newsitem.title: INDIA: Fiat unveils $1.0 billion India ventures.
newsitem.headline: Fiat unveils $1.0 billion India ventures.

text.p: Fiat SpA on Monday returned to a special relationship with India that began 90 years ago with the unveiling of plans to invest $1.0 billion over the next five years in various ventures.
Paolo Cantarella, Fiat's chief executive officer, outlined a range of new investments while addressing a gathering of Indian businessmen in the capital, New Delhi.
"The investment programmes we have launched or are now planning in this country will be worth $1.0 billion between 1997 and 2002.

"India knows and respects Fiat, and we know and respect India," he added. "More than 90 years have passed since Fiat appointed its first agent in Bombay and sold its first car. By the late 1920s, 11 percent of all cars imported into India were Fiats."
The investment will be in the group's main operating sectors, he said. These include manufacturing ventures for cars, trucks, tractors, automobile components and robotic production machinery.

"We shall be making cars in Maharashtra state; by late 1999 this plant will be producing the first of its Palio cars and once fully operational it will be turning out around 100,000 of them every year."

India in March approved a proposal for a $558 million joint venture between Fiat and India's Doshi family, which controls Premier Automobiles Ltd (PAL), to produce cars. Fiat holds 74 percent of the joint venture, Fiat India Auto Ltd.
The joint venture plans to build a new plant near the western city of Pune.
Indian analysts project the domestic car market in the world's second most populous nation to grow to around one million units in 2000/2001 (April/March) from 345,355 in 1995/96.

Cantarella said that Magneti Marelli SpA, a unit of Fiat, would set up a components manufacturing venture in Pune. Magneti is forming a joint venture with PAL for the components facility with a total investment of 250 million rupees ($7.0 million).
He said that Pune would also be home to another Fiat subsidiary, robotics company Comau SpA, which will make ultra-high tech production systems and transfer know-how to Indian motor manufacturers.
Cantarella said Fiat's tractor venture, being set up by its subsidiary, New Holland NV, would be in the northern Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
New Holland is investing $50 million in a facility on the outskirts of New Delhi that will make tractors in the 35- to 75-horsepower range.

Cantarella also said that Fiat's Iveco truck unit would join forces with India's second largest truck maker Ashok Leyland Ltd to modernise its Hosur 1 plant, and build the new Hosur 2 factory. Both plants are in the southern state of Karnataka.
Ashok Leyland and Iveco have an ongoing collaboration to make the Cargo line of trucks in India. Last year, Ashok Leyland made 10,000 Cargo trucks.

Cantarella said that Fiat's metallurgical components unit Teksid SpA had signed a memorandum of understanding with India's Kalyani group to set up a venture in the western state of Goa to manufacture cast iron components for the automotive industry.
